messages.subject: mark-recapture distance sampling
parts:
Hi,

I’d like to make analyses of mark-recapture distance sampling analyses.

My dataset is a set of observation points, each realized at the same time by two independent observers. So for each detected object I have the 10,01 or 11 possibility whether it was detected by observer 1, 2 or both. It should be a classical dataset.

 

My (basic !) questions are

-              Is  mrds R package suitable to analyses it ? If yes, is the point independence method being default option for that (method=”io”), and does the dht function can be used to make inferences on densities ?

Because when running the mrds analyses, the densities calculated are about twice the ones expected and more than two times the ones calculated for each observers … although p(0) is about 0.9 for each observer.

 

-              An another option is for me to consider the two observers as just one “super-observer” (using events 10,01 & 11 as “detected” for this super-observer and thus making assumption of g(0)=1). Would this approach yield similar results as a mrds approach ?

 

 

Thanks in advance,

 

Thibault Dieuleveut

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] mark-recapture distance sampling
parts:
Dear Thibault,

You are correct, the mrds package is exactly suited to this situation
and dht will yield estimates of density.

If you could send me the output of calling summary() on the fitted model
object off-list, I can take a look and we can report back.

best,
--dave
